nodes.summary: The equilibrium homozygosity `F* = (1 - u)² / (M - (M - 1)(1 - u)²)`. Biologically meaningful for `2 ≤ M`; its denominator is positive for `1 ≤ M` and `0 < u ≤ 1`, the hypotheses of the theorems below (`M = 1` being an algebraic extension).
nodes.title: Equilibrium homozygosity in the infinite-alleles model

nodes.summary: `F*` is a fixed point of the homozygosity recursion.
nodes.title: Equilibrium homozygosity is a fixed point of the recursion

nodes.summary: For `0 < u ≤ 1`, `F*` is the unique fixed point of the homozygosity recursion.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the equilibrium homozygosity

nodes.summary: One generation of drift and mutation in the infinite-alleles model with `M` gene copies and mutation probability `u` per copy: `F' = (1 - u)² (1/M + (1 - 1/M) F)`. The model domain is `2 ≤ M` (two distinct copies must exist) and `0 ≤ u ≤ 1`; the theorems below assume only `1 ≤ M`, and `M = 1` is an algebraic extension with no biological meaning. For `M = 0` the definition uses the junk value `1/0 = 0`.
nodes.title: Homozygosity recursion in the infinite-alleles model

nodes.summary: With `M = 2N` gene copies and mutation probability `u = θ/(4N)` (so that `θ = 4Nu`), the equilibrium homozygosity tends to `1/(1 + θ)` as `N → ∞`.
nodes.title: Kimura–Crow limit

nodes.summary: For `0 < u ≤ 1` the homozygosity converges to `F*` from every initial value `F₀`.
nodes.title: Convergence of homozygosity to equilibrium

nodes.summary: The equilibrium heterozygosity `H* = 1 - F*` tends to `θ/(1 + θ)` as `N → ∞` with `M = 2N` and `u = θ/(4N)`.
nodes.title: Limit $\theta/(1+\theta)$ of the equilibrium heterozygosity
